chunks: And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said one day to Ali (peace be upon him): Shall I not give you glad tidings? He said: Of course, may my father and mother be your sacrifice, for you have never ceased to bring tidings of every good. He said: Gabriel informed me just now of something astonishing. Ali (peace be upon him) said to him: What did he inform you of, O Messenger of Allah?

He said: He informed me that when a man from my nation sends blessings upon me and follows it with blessings upon my Ahl al-Bayt, the gates of heaven are opened for him, and the angels bless him seventy times, even if he is an erring sinner. Then his sins shed from him just as leaves shed from a tree. And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: I am at your service, My servant, and may good fortune come to you. And Allah says to His angels: O My angels! You bless him seventy times, and I bless him seven hundred times.

But when he blesses me without following it with blessings upon my Ahl al-Bayt, there are seventy veils between it and heaven, and Allah (Majestic is His Majesty) says: I am not at your service nor does good fortune come to you. O My angels! Do not bring up his supplication until he joins blessings on the Prophet with his progeny. So it will remain suspended until he follows me up with my Ahl al-Bayt.

key_terms.أهل البيت: Ahl al-Bayt — the household of the Prophet, specifically the Imams from the progeny of Ali and Fatima
key_terms.الصلاة على النبي: Salawat on the Prophet — invoking divine blessings upon the Prophet
key_terms.حجاب: Hijab — veil or barrier separating the supplication from reaching God
key_terms.عترة: 'Itra — progeny/kindred, referring specifically to the Imams from the Prophet's household
key_terms.لبيك: Labbayk — 'I am at your service', a response formula indicating divine acceptance

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for sending salawat on the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt together?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) conveys to Imam Ali (AS) a revelation from Gabriel about the critical importance of combining salawat on the Prophet with salawat on his Ahl al-Bayt. This hadith, narrated through Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishes that incomplete salawat — praising the Prophet but omitting his household — results in the prayer being rejected and suspended by seventy veils, while complete salawat opens the gates of heaven, earns seventy angelic blessings and seven hundred divine blessings, and expiates sins. The historical context is the Shia emphasis on the inseparable bond between the Prophet and his family (Ahl al-Bayt) as a theological and devotional principle.
word_analysis: and may good fortune come to you

en.bilal-muhammad: By this isnad from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from `Abdullah b. Sinan from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as). He said:

The Messenger of Allah (s) said one day to `Ali (as): Shall I not give you glad tidings? So, he said: Of course, may my mother and my father be your sacrifice. Surely, you do not stop giving glad tidings with every good thing. So, he said: Gabriel informed me of something astonishing. So, `Ali (as) said to him: What did he inform you of, O Messenger of Allah?

He said: He informed me that, when a man from my Nation blesses me and follows it up with blessing my Ahl al-Bayt, the gates of heaven open for him, and the angels bless him seventy times. If he is an erring sinner, the sins will shed from him just as leaves shed from a tree. Furthermore, Allah says: “I am at your service, My servant”; and Allah says to His angels: “O My angels! You bless him seventy times, and I bless him seven hundred times.”

If he blesses me without following it up with blessing my Ahl al-Bayt, there will be seventy veils between him and heaven; and Allah will say: “I am not at your service. O angels! Do not bring up his supplications until he follows the Prophet up with his progeny [in blessing].” So, it will remain suspended until he follows me up with my Ahl al-Bayt.
